atoms.a:
17th & 18th century
Beginnings of slavery in the US

flip.text:
1607
English settlers establish the first permanent colony: Jamestown, Virginia.

1619
The first slaves from Africa arrive in Jamestown.

18th century
Hundreds of thousands of Africans are enslaved, especially in the 18th century. They are forced to work mainly on tobacco or cotton plantations.

instruction.text: Match each event with the corresponding year.

atoms.a: Jamestown as the first English colony
Arrival of first African slaves Jamestown

instruction.text: Click the buttons to read more about the corresponding event.

flip.text:
1807
The transatlantic slave trade is officially illegal now, while the domestic trade continues.

1860
Abraham Lincoln, a Republican candidate, is elected president. He supports the emancipation of enslaved people in the US.

1861-1865
American Civil War: The southern states break away from the Union and become the Confederate States of America to protect slavery, which is central to their agricultural economy. Economic differences between North and South are a key cause of this conflict.

flip.text:
1865
The Confederates are defeated. As a result, slavery is abolished under the 13th Amendment.

1868
All former slaves are granted full US citizenship rights (14th Amendment).

1870
African-American men are allowed to vote (15th Amendment).
